The test `test_to_parquet_gcs_new_file` checks whether a DataFrame can be written to a GCS Parquet file. However, the test fails with a ValueError indicating that the size of a numpy.ndarray has changed and may indicate binary incompatibility.

Following the execution path, we find that the `to_parquet` method is called with the engine set to "fastparquet". This method calls the `write` method of the `fastparquet` implementation. The error occurs within this `write` method.

Upon closer inspection of the `to_parquet` method in the `pandas/io/parquet.py` file, we see that it uses the `get_engine` function to determine which Parquet library to use. If "auto" is specified as the engine, it will try "pyarrow" first and fall back to "fastparquet" if unavailable.

However, in this case, the error occurs when using the "fastparquet" engine. Upon further inspection of the `write` method within the `fastparquet/core.py` file, we see that it attempts to write a numpy.ndarray to Parquet format. The ValueError is raised because the size of the numpy.ndarray has changed.

This suggests that there may be an issue with the way that the "fastparquet" library handles numpy.ndarrays or how pandas interacts with this library.

Conclusion: The test `test_to_parquet_gcs_new_file` checks whether a DataFrame can be written to a GCS Parquet file using the "fastparquet" engine. However, the test fails because the size of a numpy.ndarray has changed and may indicate binary incompatibility when writing to Parquet format.

The methods that would be best locations for fixing this issue are:

pandas.io.parquet.to_parquet
fastparquet.core.write
